items.title: Red circle and slash: NO
items.simple: Regulatory signs tell you the law. You must obey them. A red circle with a slash means NO. The picture inside the circle shows what you must not do.
items.official: Regulatory signs inform you of the law; you must obey their instructions. Remember that a red circle with a slash means NO — the symbol inside the circle tells you what is prohibited.
items.mnemonic: Slash = NO. The picture shows what is banned.

items.title: Stop sign: full stop
items.simple: A red sign with 8 sides means STOP. Stop all the way at the sign, the stop line, the crosswalk, or the curb. Wait for cars and people to clear the way.
items.official: This eight-sided shape always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the sign, stop line, pedestrian crosswalk or curb. Wait for any vehicle or pedestrian to clear the way.

items.title: All Way stop: right goes first
items.simple: A sign under the stop sign may say ALL WAY or 4 WAY. Every car must stop. If two cars arrive at the same time, the car on the left waits. The car on the right goes first.
items.official: At some intersections you'll find a sign beneath the stop sign that reads "All Way" or "4 Way." At these intersections all vehicles on all roads leading into the intersection must stop. If you get to the intersection at the same time as other vehicles, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
items.mnemonic: A tie? The right goes first.

items.title: Yield sign: slow, let pass
items.simple: A triangle sign pointing down means YIELD. Slow down as you come to the intersection. Be ready to stop. Let cars, people walking, and people on bikes pass safely before you go.
items.official: Triangle (Yield): You must slow down as you come to the intersection. Be prepared to stop. Let any vehicles, pedestrians or bicyclists safely pass before you proceed.
items.mnemonic: Points down? Slow down. Let them pass.

items.title: Speed limit: top legal speed
items.simple: A speed limit sign shows the fastest speed you may drive on that road. That number is for good weather.
items.official: Speed Limit: These signs tell you the maximum legal speed that you may drive on the road where the sign is posted when weather conditions are good.
items.mnemonic: Speed limit = top speed in good weather.

items.title: Electronic speed limit signs
items.simple: Some roads have electronic speed limit signs. The number on them can change when the weather or traffic changes.
items.official: Some roads have electronic speed limit signs that change based on weather or traffic conditions.

items.title: Too fast for conditions ticket
items.simple: In rain, snow or ice, you can get a ticket for driving too fast. This can happen even if you are at or under the speed limit. Slow down in bad weather.
items.official: During rain, snow and ice, you may receive a ticket for driving too fast for the conditions even if you are driving at or less than the posted speed limit.
items.mnemonic: Rain, snow, ice? The limit can still be too fast.

items.title: Do Not Enter
items.simple: A DO NOT ENTER sign means you cannot drive that way. If you go past it, you are going the wrong way. You could crash head-on into cars coming toward you.
items.official: Do Not Enter – Wrong Way: These signs mean you cannot drive in that direction. If you drive past these signs you are going in the wrong direction and could get into a head-on crash with vehicles headed your way.

items.title: Wrong Way: what to do
items.simple: A WRONG WAY sign means you are driving the wrong direction. Right away, slow down and pull over. Then carefully turn around.
items.official: If you drive past these signs you are going in the wrong direction and could get into a head-on crash with vehicles headed your way. Immediately slow down, pull over, and cautiously turn around.

items.title: One Way
items.simple: A ONE WAY sign means all traffic on that road goes in one direction. Drive only the way the arrow points.
items.official: One Way: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
items.mnemonic: Follow the arrow. Never against it.

items.title: No Left Turn
items.simple: A left arrow inside a red circle with a slash means NO LEFT TURN. Turning left here is against the law.
items.official: No Left Turn: Left turns are against the law.

items.title: U-turn counts as two lefts
items.simple: In Virginia, a U-turn counts as two left turns. If you see a NO LEFT TURN sign, you may not make a U-turn there either.
items.official: In Virginia, U-turns are considered as two left turns and are illegal if this sign [No Left Turn] is posted.
items.mnemonic: U = 2 lefts. No left means no U.

items.title: No Right Turn
items.simple: A right arrow inside a red circle with a slash means NO RIGHT TURN. Right turns are illegal here. Do not turn right.
items.official: No Right Turn: Right turns are illegal. Do not make a right turn when you see this sign.

items.title: No U-Turn
items.simple: A U-shaped arrow inside a red circle with a slash means NO U-TURN. U-turns are illegal here. Do not turn around.
items.official: No U-Turn: U-turns are illegal. Do not make a U-turn when you see this sign.

items.title: No Turn on Red
items.simple: A NO TURN ON RED sign means you may not turn while the light is red. Wait for the light to turn green before you turn.
items.official: No Turn on Red: You may not turn on the red light. Wait for the signal to turn green.
items.mnemonic: Red means wait. Green means turn.

items.title: Do Not Pass
items.simple: A DO NOT PASS sign marks the start of a no passing zone. Do not pass cars ahead of you in your lane. This is true even if the road looks clear.
items.official: Do Not Pass: This sign marks the beginning of a no passing zone. You may not pass cars ahead of you in your lane, even if the way is clear.

items.title: Left Turn Yield on Green
items.simple: You see this sign at a traffic light. If you turn left on a green light, you do not have the right-of-way. Oncoming cars go first. Stop and look for them. Then turn with care.
items.official: Left Turn Yield on Green: This sign is used with a traffic signal. It tells you that the traffic turning left at a green light does not have the right-of-way and must yield to traffic coming from the other direction. Stop and look for oncoming traffic, then proceed with caution.
items.mnemonic: Green is not a free left. Oncoming cars go first.

items.title: Keep Right
items.simple: A KEEP RIGHT sign means an island, a median, or a barrier is ahead. Drive on the side the arrow points to.
items.official: Keep Right: A traffic island, median or barrier is ahead. Keep to the side indicated by the arrow.

items.title: Lane Use Control
items.simple: Lane use control signs show an arrow for each lane. If your lane has a turn arrow, you must turn the way that arrow points.
items.official: Lane Use Control: These signs are used where turns are required or where special turning movements are permitted for specific lanes. Traffic in the lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
items.mnemonic: Your lane's arrow is your path.

items.title: HOV lane sign
items.simple: HOV means High Occupancy Vehicle. An HOV lane is only for buses and cars with a driver and one or more riders. The sign tells you how many riders you need.
items.official: High Occupancy Vehicle: These signs indicate lanes reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver and one or more passengers as specified on the sign.
items.mnemonic: HOV = more people in the car.

items.title: Disabled Parking
items.simple: A wheelchair parking sign marks a space for people with a disabled parking permit. If you do not have a permit, do not park there.
items.official: Disabled Parking: Parking spaces marked with these signs are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

items.title: Reduced Speed Limit Ahead
items.simple: A REDUCED SPEED LIMIT AHEAD sign means the speed limit will change soon. Get ready to slow down.
items.official: Reduced Speed Limit Ahead: Prepare to reduce your speed; the speed limit is changing ahead.
items.mnemonic: AHEAD means soon. Ease off the gas.
